summary: Umar advises people to acquire knowledge and teach it, to stay humble before their teachers and students, and never to be arrogant.
Ali lists the rights a student owes a scholar, from not overburdening him with questions to honouring him in his absence.
Jameela, a slave woman of Anas, reports that Anas had perfume brought for the hands of Thaabit Bunaani, who would not be satisfied until he kissed them.
notes: Narrator's status as a Companion is not stated; treated as unsure.

summary: Ibn Abbaas recounts how, having held back for years from asking Umar about an incident, he finally asked who the two wives were who acted together against the Prophet, and Umar named Aa'isha and Hafsa.
notes: The author says the incident continues at length; the excerpt stops before the account itself.

summary: Sa'eed bin Musayyib asks Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas what the Prophet said to Ali when he appointed him deputy at Tabook, and Sa'd quotes the Prophet comparing Ali's status to that of Haaroon with Moosa.
notes: The quoted words of the Prophet are cut off after 'as Haaroon with Moosa'.

summary: Uthmaan bin Abdullaah bin Mowhab reports that when Jubayr bin Mut'im was asked about inheritance, he said he had no knowledge and sent someone to ask Umar, who praised him for saying Allaah knows best.
Mujaahid and Urwa each report that Abdullaah bin Umar, when asked about matters he did not know, simply said that he did not know.
notes: Two reports joined (Mujaahid, then Urwa), with a bibliographic reference in the middle. 'Urwa' is not identified; the text does not say which Urwa, so no approved id is given.

summary: Uqba bin Muslim says he stayed with Abdullaah bin Umar for thirty-four months and that Ibn Umar often answered 'I do not know', warning that such questions would make their backs a bridge to Jahannam.

Naafi reports that when a man asked Abdullaah bin Umar a question, Ibn Umar stayed silent for a long time, then rebuked him for thinking Allaah will not hold people to account for what they ask, and said he would answer only what he knew.

Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says a scholar should answer what he knows and otherwise say 'Allaah knows best', which is itself part of knowledge, and quotes the verse in which the Prophet is told to say he asks no payment and does not pretend.
notes: The quoted Qur'aan verse is addressed to the Prophet, so he is marked mentioned.

summary: Abdullaah bin Basheer reports that when Ali was asked a question he said he had no knowledge of it, and then said it was a comfort that he had once admitted not knowing something he did know.
notes: The line 'What a great source of comfort!' is unclear; the summary follows its literal sense. The Ibn Sa'd citation in the text is a reference and is left out.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says that when an Aalim gives up saying 'I do not know', he has reached his ruin, and the same saying is given again in a second narration.
notes: Two narrations of the same saying from Ibn Abbaas, joined by 'Another narration also states'.

summary: Makhool reports that Umar gave people tree-planting to rest them from lessons; Abdullaah bin Mus'ab reports that Umar set a limit on dowries and conceded to a woman who quoted the Qur'aan against him; Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi reports that Ali conceded to a man who corrected him; and Sa'eed bin Musayyib says Umar and Uthmaan debated sharply but always parted amicably.

people.name: Dhul Udda Qais bin Husayn Haarithi

notes: Four separate reports joined. The last line is the next section's heading and is ignored. Dhul Udda Qais is named only as a hypothetical bride's father. Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi is given with a fuller name than the approved muhammad-bin-kab, so he is left unlinked; he may be the same person. The text gives (RA), but he is generally counted a Tabi'i; please check.

summary: Uqba bin Aamir tells how he took turns minding his tribe's camels so the others could hear the Prophet, and how Umar relayed the Prophet's words on wudhu and on dying without shirk, after which the Prophet asked whether he preferred one or twelve.
notes: 'Mustahab companions' in the text looks like OCR garble; read as 'his companions'.

summary: Uthmaan bin Abul Aas, the youngest of a Thaqeef delegation, asked the Prophet to pray that he understand the Deen, and was made Ameer over his tribe; a second narration adds that the Prophet had a copy of the Qur'aan and gave it to him when he asked.
notes: Two reports joined. The author's note 'The Hadith still continues further' sits at the join.

summary: Anas says that when the Prophet narrated Ahadeeth, as many as sixty Companions would sit with him, and when he left they rehearsed what they had heard among themselves.
notes: Anas is matched to Anas bin Maalik by name only; the approved list has other Anas entries.

summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari says that after the Fajr salaah the Companions turned to the Prophet, and some asked him about the Qur'aan, others about inheritance and others about dreams.
Fudhaala bin Ubayd tells his companions to learn and teach each other, rehearse what they have learnt, and add istighfaar to their discussions.

Abu Nadhra says that when people asked Abu Sa'eed Khudri to write hadiths down, he refused, telling them to learn by memory as he had from the Prophet, and told them to rehearse hadiths among themselves because that reinforces memory.
notes: The approved list has two entries that could match Abu Nadhra: abu-nadhra (no) and abu-nadhrah (unsure). The one labelled 'no' is used here; please check.

summary: In another narration, Abu Sa'eed Khudri urges rehearsing hadiths, Ali says that without rehearsal they will be forgotten, and Ali adds that people should keep visiting one another.
notes: Several separate narrations joined ('Another narration' appears twice).

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood says that rehearsing hadiths keeps them alive, and in another narration that rehearsing knowledge of the Deen earns the reward of nafl salaah.
notes: Two narrations from Ibn Mas'ood joined by 'Another narration quotes'.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says he prefers rehearsing the knowledge of Deen for part of the night to spending the night in worship.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence after 'throughout the'.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that Umar put three questions to Ali, and Ali answered each with a saying of the Prophet about souls that either recognise or stay apart from one another, about clouds that pass over the heart so that a person forgets, and about true and false dreams; Umar said he was glad to have these answers before his death.
notes: 'O Abul Hasan' is Ali's kunya, not a separate person.

summary: Ibraheem Taymi reports that Umar, troubled that the Ummah differs although it has one Book, one Nabi and one Qiblah, asked Ibn Abbaas, who answered that differences arise when people recite the Qur'aan without knowing why its verses were revealed; Umar first rebuked him, then called him back and asked him to repeat it.
notes: The reference line (Tabraani, Haythami) is left out.

summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that when Umar asked what the orchard verse of Surah Baqarah meant and no one could say, Ibn Abbaas said it refers to deeds, and Umar agreed, explaining that a man most needs his deeds on the Day of Qiyaamah.

Ibn Abbaas recounts that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf objected to Umar letting him sit with the Badr veterans, and that when Umar asked about Surah Nasr Ibn Abbaas explained it as a sign of the Prophet's approaching death, which Umar confirmed.
In another, abbreviated narration, Ibn Abbaas says Umar consulted him alongside the senior Companions and that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf objected in the same way.
notes: Abbreviated: 'the rest of the narration is like the one above', so it is incomplete on its own. The full account is in n02786.

summary: Ibn Abbaas reports that Umar explained the Maa'idah verse against troublesome questions as relating to Muhaajireen doubts about lineage, then voiced fear that Ali might be carried away by conceit if he became Khaleefah, which Ibn Abbaas rejected by defending Ali and citing Aadam's lapse.
notes: Aadam is named in a Qur'aan quote as a prophet, not a Companion. Faatima is matched to the approved faatima entry; the text gives no more.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas says Khabbaab told Ibn Umar that Abu Hurayrah reported a reward for attending funerals, so Ibn Umar sent Khabbaab to Aa'isha to verify it, and when she confirmed it Ibn Umar said they had lost many qiraats.

Abu Hurayrah says the poor men of Suffa had no trade or farms to keep them from the Prophet, so he sought words to learn from him, and Ibn Umar tells him he knows more hadiths than they do because he stayed closer to the Prophet.

Ibn Abbaas says the Companions asked the Prophet no more than thirteen questions, all of them matters of benefit that appear in the Qur'aan, and then adds that the angels were the first to circle the Ka'bah and that several prophets are buried between the Black Stone and the Yamani corner.
notes: A second, unrelated statement about the Ka'bah and buried prophets is joined to the first.

summary: Aa'isha says the Ansaari women were the best because modesty did not stop them asking about the Deen, and Ummu Sulaym asks the Prophet whether a woman must bathe after a dream of intercourse, to which he says yes if she finds semen, adding that women are offshoots of men.
Sa'd (RA) says people used to question each other about things the Prophet mentioned, then questioned him so much that a matter which had been lawful became unlawful.
notes: Only 'Sa'd (RA)' is given, so he is not linked to an approved entry. He may be Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas, but the text does not say.

summary: Jaabir says the verses of Li'aan were revealed only because of the many questions asked; Ibn Mas'ood asks Haarith bin Qais why people ask so much, and Haarith says they want answers only to forget them, which Ibn Mas'ood affirms.
notes: 'Jaabir (RA)' is not further identified; assumed to be Jaabir bin Abdillaah, the approved entry. Several Jaabirs exist in the approved list.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar tells people never to ask about things that have not happened, because Umar used to curse those who did.
Umar says it is not permissible to ask about things that have not yet happened, because Allaah has already decreed everything that is still to happen.
Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that his father Zaid bin Thaabit would not give an opinion on a question until he had checked whether the matter had happened, and would answer only once it had.
notes: The text ends with a comma, so the sentence seems to continue. Khaarijah is matched to the approved khaarijah-bin-zaid entry, which is listed as unsure.

summary: Masrooq says that when he asked Ubay bin Ka'b about a matter, Ubay asked whether it had happened, and on hearing it had not said they should rest until it did; a second narration adds that they would then find a solution.
notes: Two narrations joined; the second begins 'Another narration adds'.

summary: Aamir reports that when Ammaar was asked about something, he asked whether it had happened, and on being told it had not, said to leave them until it did so they could apply themselves and find a solution.
notes: 'Aamir' is given without a patronymic, so not linked. The approved list has an Aamir Sha'bi and other Aamirs; left unlinked.

summary: Abu Umaama says that when a man who had profited from trading a tribe's shares came to the Prophet, the Prophet told him that learning ten verses of the Qur'aan was more profitable, and the man went to learn them.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence after 'which he reported to'.
